meta.date_display: the First of August, Two Thousand and Twenty-Six

game_of_the_day.headline: JULY GOES OUT IN GLORY: THE HUB NINE STORM CHAVEZ RAVINE, 9 TO 4, AND SEAL THE FINEST MONTH ANY BOSTON CLUB HAS EVER PLAYED
game_of_the_day.subtitle: One-and-twenty victories against but four defeats — a winning figure of .840, the best full month in all the franchise's long ledger — closed out upon the champions' own lawn, where Rafaela's seventh-inning thunder overturns a deficit, Bello bars the door with four scoreless frames, and Ohtani's homecoming circuit is rendered a footnote
game_of_the_day.body:
The calendar, not the scoreboard, supplies the marvel here. By taking the verdict at Los Angeles the Bostons closed their July at one-and-twenty wins against four defeats — a percentage of .840, the finest any month in the franchise's whole history has returned, and the most victories in a single month since the August of two thousand and four. That they sealed it in the champions' own yard, against the two-time defending titleholders and the game's best ledger, only gilds the entry.

The evening itself required some overturning. Boston built a three-nothing lead from *Jarren Duran*'s early single and a gift of two upon *Freeman*'s third-inning error, but the Angelenos clawed it back — *Freeman* atoning with a run-scoring single, and then *Shohei Ohtani*, restored to the order after a day nursing the balky left knee, hammering his four-and-twentieth home run, a two-run blow that put Los Angeles ahead 4 to 3 in the fifth. The lead survived precisely two innings. In the seventh *Ceddanne Rafaela* answered with a two-run circuit of his own, his twelfth, and the flood followed directly: *Andruw Monasterio*'s two-run double, Duran's run-scoring groundout, and by the ninth a 9-to-4 verdict with *Carlos Narváez*'s sacrifice fly for punctuation.

The pitching told its own tale of Boston's charmed season: *Ranger Suárez* made the start on his road back from the groin ailment, and *Brayan Bello* — the demoted starter reinvented as a once-a-week workhorse — finished with four scoreless innings for the victory, his third. The Fenway men, at eight-and-fifty wins, have taken three straight, hold the American's second wild-card chair, and stand six back of Tampa Bay in the East; the Dodgers, at nine-and-sixty wins against one-and-forty, still own the game's finest account and an eleven-game cushion in the National's West, but the opening engagement of this series has gone to the hottest club in the game.

news.subhead: The Bazaar, Two Days From the Bell: Minnesota Lands Kremer From Baltimore, Peralta and Mize Are Held From Their Turns, and the Skubal Pot Boils On
news.body:
The deadline tolls Monday, the third of August, at six o'clock, and the Twin Cities men are shopping like a club that means October business. A night after securing the left-handed fireman *A.J. Minter* from the Mets, Minnesota acquired the right-hander *Dean Kremer* from the Orioles for the outfield prospect *Jhomnardo Reyes*. Kremer, thirty years of age, was a stalwart of Baltimore's rotation these four seasons past — a hundred and six starts at a 3.95 figure — though the present campaign has used him roughly: a 6.50 earned-run mark across seven starts, with a quadriceps strain swallowing two months besides. Minnesota wagers on the older ledger.

Elsewhere the merchandise is being kept from harm's way: the Mets scratched *Freddy Peralta* from his scheduled turn with the deadline looming, and Detroit did likewise with *Casey Mize* — the surest sign yet that both men's valises are packed. As for the grandest prize, the wires hold that a *Tarik Skubal* trade looms and ask only when the remaining dominoes begin to fall; the Reds' *Hunter Greene*, asked whether his Cincinnati days are numbered, allowed that he does not think so — which is, of course, what everyone says in deadline week.

news.subhead: The Signing Table: Baltimore, Selling Elsewhere, Locks Its Bullpen Door Through Twenty-Eight
news.body: Even as one Oriole departed for Minnesota, the Baltimore counting-house made a purchase of its own: the right-handed reliever *Yennier Cano* has signed a two-year extension covering the twenty-seven and twenty-eight campaigns, with a club option for twenty-nine. A curious little counterpoint — a club selling a starter with one hand and buying certainty in the eighth inning with the other — and a signal that the Birds, suddenly winners of two straight and lurking but a game and a half from the wild-card table, do not regard themselves as dismantling.

news.subhead: Milestones: Caminero Reaches Thirty Circuits a Second Year Running, and the South Side Trio Thunder in Unison a Fifth Time
news.body:
*Junior Caminero*'s thirtieth home run of the season — a full-count sinker sent banging off the catwalk at Tampa Bay, projected at some four hundred and fifty feet — was the lone bright stroke of his club's evening (see the card, below), but it wrote him into select company: a second consecutive season of thirty circuits, a feat managed by only one Ray before him (*Carlos Peña*, in the aughts), and only *José Canseco* among Tampa men had ever reached thirty before July's close. Six men in all the game now stand at thirty or better: *Alvarez* with five-and-thirty, *Schwarber* three-and-thirty, *Goodman* and *Rice* one-and-thirty apiece, and *Wood* and Caminero at the round figure.

Across the diamond that same evening, Chicago's *Murakami*, *Vargas*, and *Montgomery* all struck home runs in the same game for the fifth time this season — a habit of collective thunder that has carried the White Stockings to the Central's penthouse.

news.subhead: The Infirmary Ward: McClanahan's Back, Contreras's Helmet, Crawford's Wrist
news.body: Tampa Bay breathes easier than it feared: the club is hopeful *Shane McClanahan*'s recurring back complaint requires only a brief stay upon the injured list. In Los Angeles, Boston's *Willson Contreras* was struck upon the helmet by a fastball of ninety-five miles in the third inning and left the field as a precaution — the club termed it nothing graver, though the Herald notes such verdicts belong to the morning after. Seattle placed *J.P. Crawford* on the ten-day list with inflammation of the left wrist, and the Cubs shelved the reliever *Gavin Hollowell* (right shoulder) whilst recalling the left-hander *Antoine Kelly* — with the closer *Palencia* said to be nearing his return.

news.subhead: The Counting-House Curiosity: San Francisco Stops Bader's Pay Over a Scooter Misadventure
news.body: The Giants have suspended payment upon the salary of the outfielder *Harrison Bader*, who aggravated his already-injured left foot in a scooter accident this past weekend. The Herald offers no opinion on the actuarial merits, save to observe that the injured list has been reached by stranger conveyances, and that a man drawing a ballplayer's wage might reasonably be asked to leave the scooters to the delivery trade.

rest_of_the_card.headline: TWO SWINGS SUFFICE AT WRIGLEY: WARREN AND THE BOMBERS BLANK THE CUBS, 2 TO 0, IN A MEETING OF EQUALS
rest_of_the_card.body: Two nines level at two-and-sixty wins apiece met in the Friday sunshine, and the Highlanders' *Will Warren* owned the afternoon: six-and-two-thirds scoreless frames, seven strikeouts, and not a single pass issued. *Amed Rosario* and the young *Spencer Jones* supplied solo circuits in the fourth and fifth off the unfortunate *Imanaga*, and *Bednar* sealed his three-and-twentieth save. New York banks a second wind after two extra-inning heartbreaks at Chicago's other yard; the Bruins drop the opener but hold the National's first wild-card chair regardless.

rest_of_the_card.headline: STEWART GIVETH, AND STEWART GIVETH AGAIN: THE RED STOCKINGS OUTLAST PITTSBURGH, 8 TO 7, IN A PROPER QUEEN CITY SEESAW
rest_of_the_card.body: Down early and pressed late, the Cincinnatis leaned twice upon young *Sal Stewart*: a two-run circuit in the fourth, his three-and-twentieth, that broke a three-all knot, and a two-run single in the eighth that squared the account at seven after the Buccaneers had plated three to seize a 7-to-5 edge. The winning run followed on the humblest instrument yet: *Nathaniel Lowe*'s fielder's choice, aided by a Pittsburgh misplay. Stewart's four runs batted in swell his account to four-and-eighty, the National's best; *Pagán* took the win, and the Smoky City men have now dropped four running. *Jake Mangum* homered, stole his twentieth base, and drove in two in a losing cause.

rest_of_the_card.headline: HENDERSON'S TRIPLE TURNS THE SEVENTH, AND PHILADELPHIA'S SLIDE REACHES FOUR: ORIOLES 6, PHILLIES 4
rest_of_the_card.body: The Quakers led 4 to 2 on circuits by *Trea Turner* and *Realmuto*, whereupon the seventh inning undid them entire: *Encarnacion-Strand*'s two-run double squared the account and *Gunnar Henderson*'s two-run triple settled it, the loss charged to *Kerkering*, lately unbeaten at six victories. *Alonso*'s two-run blow, his three-and-twentieth, had kept Baltimore in the hunt from the first. The Birds have won two straight and creep within a game and a half of the American's last wild-card chair; Philadelphia, two victories in its last ten, clings to the National's final chair by a bare game over San Diego.

rest_of_the_card.headline: OKAMOTO AND URÍAS DO THE QUIET COMMERCE: THE MAPLE LEAF NINE TOP ST. LOUIS, 3 TO 1
rest_of_the_card.body: *Kazuma Okamoto* doubled home the equalizer in the sixth and *Luis Urías* singled two across in the eighth, and that modest ledger sufficed. *Hoffman* took the win, *Varland* his four-and-twentieth save, and the Mound City men — who led on *Jordan Walker*'s ninth-and-seventieth run batted in — managed nothing further and have now lost two straight, slipping below the even mark at four-and-fifty wins.

rest_of_the_card.headline: THREE SINGLES IN THE EIGHTH, ALL OF THEM DAGGERS: THE DESERT NINE TAKE CLEVELAND, 4 TO 1, AND TIGHTEN THEIR WILD-CARD GRIP
rest_of_the_card.body: For seven innings *Rhys Hoskins*'s first-frame single stood as the whole of the scoring; then Arizona strung the eighth together like beads — run-scoring singles by *Perdomo*, *Moreno* (two crossing on an outfield misplay), and *Ketel Marte* — and the Lake Erie men were undone. *Loáisiga* won it, *Bibee* absorbed his eleventh defeat, and *Garcia* closed the door. The Snakes, winners of three straight, hold the National's second wild-card chair; Cleveland's loss drops them level with Minnesota for the American's last one.

rest_of_the_card.headline: FOUR CIRCUITS FLY THE SOUTH SIDE FLAG: WHITE SOX 6, RAYS 1, IN THE MEETING OF FIRST-PLACE MEN
rest_of_the_card.body: The Central leaders called upon the East leaders and settled matters by air mail: *Vargas*, *Benintendi*, *Murakami* (two aboard), and *Colson Montgomery* (likewise) all homered, Montgomery's five-and-twentieth drawing him level among the American's leading sluggers. *Fedde* scattered the Sunshine nine's offerings and pinned the loss on *Martinez*, ten victories against now three defeats. *Caminero*'s thirtieth (see the milestones, above) was Tampa Bay's lone answer. Chicago has won three straight; the Rays' Eastern cushion holds at two games and a half.

rest_of_the_card.headline: A FOUR-RUN FIFTH SINKS FLUSHING: MARLINS 5, METS 2, AND SENGA'S WINLESS SEASON REACHES EIGHT DEFEATS
rest_of_the_card.body: The Fish did all their commerce in one frame — *Marsee*'s double, *Joe Mack*'s two-run single, and *Edwards*'s knock making it four — and *Kyle Stowers*'s sixteenth circuit supplied the garnish. *Junk* took the verdict, *Fairbanks* his sixteenth save, and poor *Senga* fell to naught-and-eight. *Lindor* homered in consolation. The Floridians thereby stay but a game and a half off the wild-card pace; the Metropolitans, at seven-and-forty wins, play out the string and mind Monday's bazaar.

rest_of_the_card.headline: OLSON AND HARRIS SUPPLY THE ARTILLERY: THE ATLANTAS TURN BACK WASHINGTON, 6 TO 2, AND GRIFFIN'S CHARMED SEASON TAKES A THIRD LOSS
rest_of_the_card.body: *Matt Olson* opened the scoring with his nine-and-twentieth circuit and *Michael Harris II* closed the argument with a three-run blow in the sixth, his twentieth, while the rookie *Jim Jarvis* chipped in two singles worth a pair of runs. *Elder* took the win; *Griffin*, Washington's twelve-game winner, the defeat. *CJ Abrams* struck his eight-and-twentieth homer — his three-and-eightieth run driven in, second in the National — in a losing cause. The East leaders, at five-and-sixty wins, sit eight clear of the field.

rest_of_the_card.headline: THE WEST CHANGES HANDS: HOUSTON BATTERS TEXAS, 11 TO 2, AND SEIZES THE DIVISION'S CHAIR BY HALF A GAME
rest_of_the_card.body: The 'Stros treated their neighbors roughly for the fourth night running of this splendid stretch — nine victories in ten — piling up eleven runs on circuits by *Paredes*, *Walker*, and *Diaz*, three runs batted in from *Jeremy Peña*, and two more from *Yordan Alvarez*, whose two-and-eighty now lead all the game. *Brown* took the win; *Eovaldi*, the defeat. With the verdict Houston passes Arlington for the West's top chair by half a game and pockets the season's series against its rival besides. *Pederson*'s twentieth homer was the visitors' consolation.

rest_of_the_card.headline: SUGANO RUNS HIS ACCOUNT TO ELEVEN IN THE THIN AIR: ROCKIES 3, ROYALS 1
rest_of_the_card.body: The Mile High nine's *Tomoyuki Sugano* — eleven victories now for a club with but three-and-forty — turned in the quiet masterwork of the evening, and *Rumfield*'s single, an error-gifted run, and *Brenton Doyle*'s double built the modest margin. *Romano* sealed his ninth save. The young receiver *Carter Jensen*'s fifteenth home run was the whole of the Royal blues' reply; they have dropped two straight.

rest_of_the_card.headline: TURANG AND BAUERS MAKE SHORT WORK OF THE SERAPHS: BREWERS 6, ANGELS 2, TO OPEN THE LONG MARCH
rest_of_the_card.body: The Cream City nine began what the wires style a seventeen-day gauntlet without a day's rest in businesslike fashion: *Brice Turang*'s two-run circuit and *Jake Bauers*'s three-run blow arrived in the same five-run fifth inning, all of it behind *Drohan*'s steady work. *Denzer Guzman*'s two-run homer was Anaheim's lot; the Halos have lost four straight. Milwaukee, at eight-and-sixty wins, keeps its six-and-a-half-game hold on the Central.

rest_of_the_card.headline: THE DEBUTANTE STEALS THE SHOW, AND DINGLER SUPPLIES THE EXCLAMATION: TIGERS 13, ATHLETICS 1
rest_of_the_card.body: *Max Clark*, summoned at last from Toledo, struck three hits in his first major-league engagement — a pair of doubles among them — and the Detroits fairly buried the White Elephants beneath a six-run eighth and a four-run ninth. *Dillon Dingler*'s grand slam, his three-and-twentieth circuit, ran his runs batted in to two-and-seventy, third in the American; *Kevin McGonigle* homered besides; *Javier Báez* drove in three; and *Ben Malgeri* struck the first home run of his young life. *Madden* took the first victory of his own. The Elephants, beaten a third straight time, offered *Heim*'s early double and little else.

rest_of_the_card.headline: MATSUI AND COMPANY HANG THE WHITEWASH: FRIARS 7, JINTS 0, AND FRANCE DRIVES IN THREE
rest_of_the_card.body: San Diego's arms permitted the Bay nine nothing whatever, *Matsui* taking the win in the combined shutout, while *Ty France* batted in three, *Tatis Jr.* doubled and stole his six-and-twentieth base, and young *Jase Bowen* struck the first circuit of his career. *Whisenhunt* bore the defeat. The Friars, winners of seven in their last ten, close within a single game of the National's last wild-card chair — the Quakers may check the standings with their coffee — whilst San Francisco sinks sixteen below the even mark.

rest_of_the_card.headline: JEFFERS HAS THE LAST WORD IN THE EIGHTH: TWINS 5, MARINERS 3, AND THE DEADLINE SHOPPERS KEEP WINNING
rest_of_the_card.body: Twice Seattle held the upper hand — *Cal Raleigh*'s two-run double in the first, *Cole Young*'s go-ahead circuit in the second — and twice the North Stars clawed back level before pulling clear: *Brooks Lee*'s two-run homer, *Royce Lewis*'s equalizer in the seventh, *Keaschall*'s go-ahead double directly after, and *Ryan Jeffers*'s eighth-inning blast for daylight. *Funderburk* won it and *Gómez* sealed his fourteenth save. Minnesota, busy at the bazaar (see above), has won two straight and sits level with Cleveland for the American's final wild-card chair; the mariners of the Sound have dropped three running, two victories in their last ten.

desk_note: Two days remain before Monday's bell — the third of August, at six o'clock — and this evening's card runs fifteen games strong. The White Stockings and the Sunshine nine renew their first-place quarrel at ten past four, *Hicks* opposite *Rasmussen*; *Sánchez*, the National's winningest arm at thirteen victories, takes the hill for Philadelphia at Baltimore at five past seven; *deGrom* answers for Texas at Houston at ten past seven with the West's chair now in dispute by half a game; the Yankees and Cubs, level at two-and-sixty wins apiece, resume at Wrigley at a quarter past seven, *Fried* against *Peterson*; and by late lamplight Boston sends *Tolle* against *Yamamoto* at Chavez Ravine, ten past nine, to learn whether August can be made to resemble July. Until the next dispatch, keep your scorecards near and your enthusiasms nearer.
